parsed.n_justification: A single ELM column cannot represent lateral flow convergence or inter-position groundwater exchange. We discretize one representative Naches hillslope into 4 hydrologically-connected columns spanning the HAND (Height-Above-Nearest-Drainage) sequence — ridge/upland, upper mid-slope, lower mid-slope, and riparian/toeslope adjacent to the stream — enabling ELM hillslope hydrology lateral subsurface routing and downslope groundwater exchange while keeping the configuration runnable and interpretable.
requires_capabilities: ELM hillslope hydrology module (use_hillslope=.true.) with HAND-based column discretization and inter-column lateral saturated/unsaturated flow
Lateral subsurface flow and downslope groundwater exchange between hillslope columns
Topographic preprocessing: DEM-derived HAND, flowpath length, slope, and column geometry from the 352-1977 m elevation range
PFLOTRAN coupling (ELM-PFLOTRAN) for higher-fidelity 3D saturated groundwater exchange between neighboring hillslope positions
Offline travel-time post-processing (flux-weighted or particle-tracking) using ELM lateral flux, effective porosity, and flowpath length
assumptions: Topography is the only available driver; atmospheric forcing uses the standard GSWP3/CLMNCEP dataset (1980-2018) since no site meteorology was provided
The 4-column sequence represents one characteristic Naches forested hillslope; results are relative/process-level, not basin-integrated
Soil textures assigned by typical downslope fining (coarse ridge to silty riparian); should be refined with SSURGO/gridded soils if available
Travel times are derived offline from simulated lateral fluxes and geometry — ELM does not output travel-time distributions natively
Full 3D neighbor-to-neighbor groundwater exchange beyond the resolved hillslope requires PFLOTRAN; the pure ELM hillslope module approximates it as downslope column-to-column routing
A multi-year spin-up (recycle forcing) precedes the 1980-2018 transient run to equilibrate water table and aquifer storage
